Because the image only contains a single dimension (13 cm) and no scale, I cannot derive exact finished pattern dimensions, but I can give you the geometric drafting formulas used by bespoke trousermakers.

1. Waistband Length Formula

The finished waistband length equals the trouser waist line plus overlap.

WL=W+OWL = W + O

Where:

WLWL = waistband length
WW = trouser waist circumference
OO = overlap extension

Typical bespoke overlap:

O=3.5 cm to 5.0 cmO = 3.5 \text{ cm to } 5.0 \text{ cm}

Example:

Waist = 84 cm

WL=84+4=88 cmWL = 84 + 4 = 88 \text{ cm}
2. Waistband Width Formula

Finished width:

WWf=3.5 cm to 4.5 cmWW_f = 3.5 \text{ cm to } 4.5 \text{ cm}

Cut width before folding:

WWc=(WWf×2)+SAWW_c = (WW_f \times 2) + SA

Where:

SASA = seam allowances

Example:

Finished waistband = 4 cm

WWc=(4×2)+2WW_c = (4 \times 2) + 2 WWc=10 cmWW_c = 10 \text{ cm}
3. Extension Tab Geometry

For a classic bespoke extension:

EL=0.04W+1EL = 0.04W + 1

ELEL = extension length

4. Fly Extension Formula

The underlap extension behind the zipper is typically:

FE=Zw+1.5FE = Z_w + 1.5

Where:

FEFE = fly extension width
ZwZ_w = zipper tape width

Typical:

FE=4.0−4.5 cmFE = 4.0 - 4.5 \text{ cm}
